meta.description: Kickoff 47's Part B (finding 13): its 24 circuits, instruction by instruction, reconstructed on 10 October 2026 by running the run's own builder again; not the circuits as sent, which were not saved. The run's counts, and the operation counts recorded from the circuits as sent (part_B_circuits), are in the released archive, ibm_fez/k47-wait.json, which this file leaves unchanged. Every circuit's operation counts here equal those. Instruction-by-instruction identity with the circuits as sent cannot be checked. The builder's Part B text is included, so the reconstruction can be repeated (meta.builder).
meta.label: reconstructed on 10 October 2026 by rerunning the original builder; not the circuits as sent
meta.utc_note: the run's time; the reconstruction was made on reconstructed_on

environment.translation: in the builder: Qiskit's preset pass manager at optimization level 0, the group as the initial layout, seed_transpiler 47

builder.what: verbatim from the run's script: the Part B function (build_B) and what it needs (GROUPS, TAUS_US, tau_dt), and Part B's run order (b_list); nothing of Part A
builder.how_to_repeat: Run the text in a fresh namespace and call build_B on qiskit-ibm-runtime's offline ibm_fez snapshot (FakeFez). Record each circuit of the first value it returns with manacitra.wait.structure; its key (group, tau_us, variant) names the entry g{group}|{tau_us}|{variant} in circuits. b_list() gives the order the run sent them in: the 24, then the same in reverse (the second copy). tests/test_wait.py does this.
builder.scanned: the identifier scan (tools/scan_secrets.py) passed on the text before it was added

meta.circuits_format: each instruction as [name, physical qubits, classical bits, parameters]; a delay's parameter is its length in dt
meta.circuits_sha256_of: the circuits block as compact JSON with sorted keys (json.dumps(circuits, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':')))
